report.say:
The Gandalf-heavy deep read did not run — the step timed out. What actually happened is that the researchPrime host loaded a *different* commission: the BA 815 assessment-structure decision-support directive (policy, SDR route, pricing, weight table), and it treated the deep read as already delivered on disk (`research/DEEP-READ-AGENT-IMPL.md`), explicitly noting it was NOT re-run. So no new deep-read verdict, no fresh deck inventory, no session/lecture/quiz counts from this run.

What it did produce before the timeout is substantial and worth keeping: a frozen plan (`PLAN.md`, planHash b627e6f9), and a six-branch evidence draft through three adversarial rounds. Highlights — AD40 governs recording but is silent on exams and only says "should inform"; PA is all-party consent (18 Pa.C.S. §5704(4)), and no PSU consent instrument exists. Exam audio is a FERPA education record, with a 45-day inspection right under 34 CFR 99.10 colliding with AD11's 60-day vendor destruction rule. PSU's AI Guidelines require instructor grade verification plus department-head *and* dean approval for AI-assisted grading (47-20, G-10 exposure). The 2025 seven-name accommodation list is expired by design — zero types on file is expected. Pricing was corrected: the $3/exam figure is NYU-reported, not a quote; rate-true is $3.30, and the honest envelope is ≤$1,105 (2 sittings) / ≤$1,505 (3). A round-2 skeptic refuted the "Copilot-only" claim — AI Studio, Gemini, and Copilot are all PSU-provided and marked OK for course grades.

The run never rendered the final one-pager.

reflection.impact: The deep read didn't run — but it already exists on disk twice (Gandalf's graded verdict run-1786112467156 and researchPrime's 08-07 re-derivation), so re-commissioning would buy a third read of unchanged material; I'm treating it as delivered pending your ledger call. The real change: assessment-policy jumped from proposed to nearly decision-ready — recording consent, the FERPA/AD11 retention collision, the dean-level approval chain, and an honest pricing ceiling (≤$1,505) are now evidence-graded on disk. What's missing is the final one-pager (lost to timeout) and two decisive unknowns: Level-3 data classification and Smeal-side sources. Separately: the machinery loaded the wrong directive — the second brief-delivery fault in two runs; routing needs an eye before heavier commissions.

next.directive: Finish the BA 815 assessment-structure decision-support deliverable from the existing artifacts in research/rp-assess-a00e50e9/ — the frozen PLAN.md (planHash b627e6f9) and DELIVERABLE-DRAFT.md v2 (branches B1–B6 plus the DECISION REGISTER) stand; do not re-derive settled branches. Close only the named gaps: (1) whether exam audio is Level 3 data under AD53 / PSU's data-classification standard — this gates the platform fork between the PSU-provided trio (AI Studio, Gemini, Copilot, all marked OK for course grades) and any external vendor under AD11; (2) Smeal-side policy material — smeal.psu.edu failed TLS twice, so route via web archive or the university bulletin; (3) voice-exam fitness and enterprise pricing of the PSU-provided platforms, where fetchable. Then render the final one-pager: per-branch recommendation, the 7-item decision register for John, and the approvals-timing queue (dept-head + dean email; SDR pre-semester consultation) as dated lead times.
next.why: The decision register is what unlocks weights, project shape, and tool track — syllabus, homework, and the oral-exam engine all plan FROM those decisions. Handing John an incomplete brief means he decides twice, or decides the platform fork blind on the Level-3 question. And the approval queues (dean email, SDR consultation) are calendar items with lead times — every week they stay unfired compresses the three block-rebuild steps at the end of the campaign.

oranges: Commission routing is now the campaign's biggest waste vector: two consecutive delivery faults (a mangled brief, then the wrong directive loaded against the commissioned step). Every misfire burns a run and a day — verify the step→brief binding before commissioning Crucible or Foreman, whose runs cost far more to lose.

The compliance chain has queues, not just paperwork: dept-head+dean approval for AI-assisted grading and the SDR pre-semester consultation must fire the moment the decision register is answered — if they fire after the syllabus is drafted, the oral-exam design may have to be walked back mid-build.

The FERPA 45-day inspection right versus AD11's 60-day vendor destruction makes audio retention a contract term, not an implementation detail — any vendor or platform commitment made before retention terms are set gets renegotiated later, at worst mid-semester with live exam records.
